sessions.text:
User: My feature branch is a few commits behind main and I'm never sure what the cleanest way to sync is.
Assistant: There are a couple of options. Do you have a general preference for how branches get integrated, or a preference for how I format git instructions?
User: In general, I prefer rebasing feature branches onto main over merge commits. Also, always put a one-line comment above every git command explaining what it does.
Assistant: Got it. I'll default to rebasing and I'll comment every command.
User: Perfect. I'll come back when I have the next branch to sort out.

User: I just got access to Project Helios, a telemetry dashboard with a big shared repo.
Assistant: Welcome aboard. Anything about the git workflow I should keep in mind?
User: On Project Helios, bring branches up to date with merge commits. Several of us push to the same feature branches, so history rewrites cause trouble.
Assistant: Understood. On Project Helios I'll use merge commits when syncing a branch with main.
User: Thanks. That's all for now.
